newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's LPMO buys 9,458 tonnes frozen beef - trade.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's LPMO buys 9,458 tonnes frozen beef - trade.

text.p: South Korea's Livestock Products Marketing Organization (LPMO) on Friday bought a total of 9,458 tonnes of frozen beef from four countries, traders said.
The organization bought 5,188 tonnes from Australia, 3,704 tonnes from the United States, 440 tonnes from New Zealand and 126 tonnes from Canada, they said.

U.S. and Canadian chuck roll was bought at $3,128-$3,480 per tonne and short-rib at $3,075-$3,309. Australian and New Zealand grain-fed bone-in beef was bought at $2,371-$2,406, grass-fed fullset at $2,638-$2,747 and grass-fed bone-in beef at up to $1,767, they said. All prices are on a cost and freight basis.
Officials at the government-controlled organisation could not immediately be reached for comment.
Arrivals were set for Seoul, Pusan, Taegu and Naju. Shipment of 4,030 tonnes was slated for December 10, that of 4,048 tonnes for December 20 and that of 1,380 tonnes for December 30.
